evidence.source: Development fast-lane rollout run 31114548204 (run number 45), workflow_dispatch on main at head a90eb2e4f37f97fab554d6e97564dcc38b68015b, applying contracts 123, 124 and 125 in one run. THE RUN IS THE EVIDENCE AND ITS OWN LOGS HOLD THE OBJECT-LEVEL DETAIL: the lane refused an unsafe dispatch, preflighted the development secret, derived the pending set and proved each migration additive by reading it, took a pre-apply snapshot, applied, and confirmed hosted development matched the repository. Every step reported success and the connection-failure step was skipped, so the credential that this document has twice guessed about is working. INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMED AFTER THE RUN, not inferred from it: the Supabase management API was queried directly for project iouzoutneyjpugbbtdem and returned 125 applied migrations ending at 20260806160000_season_fixture_result_entry, which is the repository's own latest. That is a second reading of the target rather than a second reading of the workflow. CONTRACT 124 WAS THE FIRST STRUCTURAL MIGRATION THIS LANE HAS CARRIED: it drops and re-adds bonus_cup_groups_size_allowed so a split half may hold two entrants. The additive checker classified it as structural rather than destructive — no row is lost and the guarantee returns in the next statement — and reported it rather than passing it in silence, which is the handling that category was added for. WHAT THIS RECORD DOES NOT CLAIM: no object-level hash, grant, RLS or cron assertion was re-derived here. Those belong to the run's logs and snapshot artifact, and to the pgTAP suites that shipped with each contract — 175, 176 and 177 all passed on the merged commit before it was applied anywhere.
